name: LCI INDUSTRIES

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest case for modelling LCII anyway is that an all-stock merger is not a cash-out: an LCI holder ends up owning 48% of a real operating business, so the underlying cash flows still matter and refusing to value them is intellectually lazy. And the deal could break — it needs two shareholder votes and an antitrust review of a combination of the two largest RV component suppliers, which is a real concentration question. If it breaks, LCI's standalone value is exactly what the engine is trying to compute.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Antitrust clearance or a second request from the FTC; the S-4 becoming effective and both shareholder votes scheduled; and the deal spread. If the spread widens materially against 1.2440 times Patrick's price, the market is pricing break risk and standalone value becomes the live question again.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Partly, and it cuts against modelling it. The board approvals were unanimous on both sides, the structure is a merger of near-equals (52/48) rather than a premium takeout, and LCII's 5-day and 21-day moves of -9.0% and -12.0% are ordinary dispersion — which is exactly the BKH signature in LESSONS.md: in a share exchange the price floats with the ACQUIRER, so the tape looks normal and neither the SLAB pinned-price tell nor the APGE items 3.01/5.01 tell fires. What I could not check is the current Patrick share price against the 1.2440 ratio, so I cannot quantify the spread and therefore cannot quantify the implied break probability.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The antitrust path. A combination of LCI and Patrick is a combination of the two dominant suppliers of RV components to the same Elkhart OEM customer base, and I did not find any disclosure of the HSR status. That is the one thing that would return this name to a standalone valuation question, and I could not resolve it.

what_changed: Everything the model does not know. (1) The merger: announced 2026-06-30, confirmed in the 8-K filed 2026-09-10 under Item 8.01 reporting an event dated 2026-09-04, which recites the Merger Agreement with Patrick Industries, Planet First Merger Sub Inc. and Planet Second Merger Sub LLC — a two-step structure with LCI surviving first as a Patrick subsidiary and then merging into the second sub. The cluster of Item 8.01/9.01 8-Ks on 2026-07-22, 2026-08-07, 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-10 with no 2.02 among them is the merger-communications pattern. (2) The business, which is in a genuine downturn: Q2 2026 adjusted net sales fell 4.5% to $1,057.5 million; the company LOWERED 2026 North American RV wholesale shipment guidance to 280,000-300,000 units from 315,000-330,000; July net sales were approximately $315 million, down 4%. Operating margin guidance of 7.5-8.0% was reaffirmed on self-help cost actions, and adjusted EPS rose 13% to $2.70 on a 4% sales decline. The company also paid off the remaining $92.0 million of its 2026 convertible notes at maturity in the first half.
consensus_case: There is no standalone consensus to steelman, because LCI Industries has agreed to be acquired. On 30 June 2026 LCII entered an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Patrick Industries under which each LCI share converts into 1.2440 Patrick shares, with legacy Patrick holders owning about 52% of the combined company and LCI holders about 48%. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to both shareholder votes and regulatory approval, with more than $150 million of run-rate cost synergies targeted within three years. At $93.40 the shares imply a Patrick price of about $75.08, so what the market is 'assuming' about LCI's cash flows is only its assumption about Patrick's, plus a deal-completion probability.
base_case_rationale: I will not supply one. A five-year FCFF growth rate for a standalone LCI Industries is a number about a company that has contracted to stop existing in the first half of 2027. Supplying it would launder a category error into a fair value, which is the discipline the PIPR entry in LESSONS.md establishes.
key_risks: The engine will keep running a standalone DCF on LCII every session until it delists in 2027, exactly as it is still doing on BKH — this is the second pending all-stock merger to reach the briefs in three sessions
If the merger breaks, the standalone case is a supplier into RV wholesale shipments just guided down 11% with July sales -4%
Antitrust review of the two largest RV component suppliers combining is unquantified here
The +208% gap that won this an opportunistic slot is built on a trough FCFF base in an RV downturn AND on a company that has agreed to be acquired — two independent reasons the number is meaningless
watch_for: S-4 effectiveness and the scheduling of both shareholder votes
Any FTC second request on the Patrick/LCI combination
The deal spread against 1.2440 x PATK widening beyond a few percent
Termination of the Merger Agreement — the only event that makes a standalone valuation of LCII meaningful again
